passage:
"You lost the whole game because you're a baby," Binita said. "Even Mumma says you can't lose properly."
"I'm not a baby." Tenzin's voice shook.
"Baby, baby. Look, his ears have gone red."
"Stop it!"
"Why? You always—"
"STOP!" Tenzin's hands felt hot, and his heart thumped so hard he could hear it. He shoved the board, and the pieces flew across the rug.
"Mumma! He threw everything!"
Mumma came in from the kitchen. "Tenzin—"
But Tenzin was already running to the bedroom. The door banged. Inside, he sat against the bed, breathing fast, face burning, not even sure what he had just done.
"He always does this," Binita said.
"Let him breathe first," Mumma said quietly.

qa.q: What did Tenzin do to the board game?
qa.a: He shoved the board, and the pieces flew across the rug.

qa.q: What shows that Tenzin felt overwhelmed rather than choosing to throw the game?
qa.a: His hands felt hot, his heart thumped so hard he could hear it, and afterwards he was not even sure what he had just done.

qa.q: What does Mumma get right at this stage, and what could come next?
qa.a: She lets Tenzin breathe first instead of scolding; once he is calm she can hear both children and deal with the teasing too.

qa.q: How does Binita see what happened?
qa.a: Binita sees Tenzin as the troublemaker, saying "He always does this", without linking the shove to the teasing.

grounding: Shows a teased child whose body takes over, with a pounding heart and hot face, shoving the game and running off without a real choice.

passage: Last week I cried in the art room, and I still don't really know how it happened. I'm ten, and I hadn't cried at school since I was a small boy. Kashish kept laughing at my drawing of a horse. "It looks like a dog with a long neck," Kashish said, and then everybody at our table started saying it. I tried to say something clever back. But my heart was going so fast, and my face got so hot, that my brain just went blank. No words came. Tears came instead, big ones, in front of everyone. I pushed my chair back and walked out to the corridor. I didn't decide to. My legs just went. Later, Miss Rao found me by the drinking fountain and waited with me till I could breathe normally again. — Sachin

qa.q: What did Kashish say Sachin's horse looked like?
qa.a: Kashish said it looked like a dog with a long neck.

qa.q: How did Sachin feel when he said "My legs just went"?
qa.a: He felt hurt and overwhelmed, with his heart racing and his face hot, so his body walked him out before he could decide. 😔

qa.q: What did Miss Rao do that helped, and what could come next?
qa.a: Miss Rao stayed with Sachin until his breathing settled; next the teacher could talk calmly with both children about the teasing.

qa.q: What might Kashish have thought when Sachin walked out?
qa.a: Kashish may have been surprised, thinking it was only a joke, and not realised how much the laughing from the whole table hurt.

grounding: Shows a boy on the receiving end of teasing whose racing heart and hot face leave him unable to think, so he cries and walks out.
